title: The exceptional inverse image
statement:
Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb\}$ be an admissible coefficient
ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of the standing schemes (separated and of finite type
over the standing field $k$, with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$; [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]).

1. The objects of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ ([sk-def-sfb-constructible]) are compact in
   $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ ([sk-def-localizing-closure]) and a small skeleton compactly
   generates it.
2. Compactifications define an exact functor
   $Rf_!\colon\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$, preserving direct sums and
   sending $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ (compare [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek]).
3. A single application of Brown representability gives an exact right adjoint
   $f^!\colon\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.
4. This right adjoint sends $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, so its adjunction
   restricts to $\Dctf$.

For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$ one has $\Dctf=\Dbc$, so the theorem
holds with $\Dbc$ in place of $\Dctf$. The finite ring $A$ is arbitrary; it need not be
regular or Gorenstein. The $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ cases are the integral and
rational cases with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

proof.text: Both schemes are qcqs by the cited affine-base lemma applied to their separated finite-type structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: (2): qcqs hypotheses for compactification and coherence

proof.text: Write $a_X=a_Yf$. Separated cancellation gives $f$ separated; finite-type permanence (f) gives $f$ locally of finite type. Since $X$ is quasi-compact and $Y$ quasi-separated, quasi-compact permanence (1) gives $f$ quasi-compact, hence of finite type.

source.place: (2): separated finite-type hypothesis; the detailed verification in sk-def-sfb-dc-setting/lem-sfb-compactification-over-base.proof.md

proof.text: Brown hypotheses applied to $X$ and $Y$ give their triangulated localizing closures with ambient sums, compactness of $\Dctf$, and a small skeleton of compact generators. This proves (1).
Nagata applies by steps 1–2. Fix its dense compactification $f=pj$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper.
For this compactification, the single-compactification theorem restricts $Rp_*j_!$ to an exact functor between these closures, preserving sums and $\Dctf$. Denote it by $Rf_!$.
The coherence theorem compares this $Rf_!$ with every other compactification, independently of refinement, with identity and cocycle laws. Thus (2) holds.
Apply the general existence theorem once to this same compactification functor. Its Brown adjunction gives an exact right adjoint $f^!$, proving (3).
For finite $A$, the finite-coefficient preservation theorem applies to this general Brown adjoint and gives $f^!(\Dctf(Y,A))\subseteq\Dctf(X,A)$.
For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, the integral Brown identification identifies this adjunction with the integral one. Integral restriction therefore gives preservation of $\Dctf$ for the same $f^!$.
For $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, rational restriction gives preservation of $\Dctf$ for this same general Brown adjoint.

source.place: field-coefficient bullet and introductory coefficient specializations

proof.text: The base-coefficient identification gives $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\cong\underline{\mathcal O}_{E_0}$ and $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\cong\underline{E_0}$ for the bottom finite subextension $E_0$. Coefficient-isomorphism transport identifies the compactification functors and their given right adjoints. Thus steps 9–10 give preservation for $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ too.

source.place: Introduction, coefficient specializations, with the scalar identifications and adjoint comparisons separated as independent tasks.

proof.text: Both functors now preserve the full $\Dctf$ subcategories. Apply fully faithful adjunction restriction to their inclusions and the identity comparison isomorphisms. The resulting Hom bijections, unit and counit give (4).

source.place: final paragraph: formal restriction of the adjunction

proof.text: For the five non-finite coefficients, the cited equality theorem applies to the qcqs schemes of step 1: $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and their localizing closures agree. Substitution gives the claimed $\Dbc$ version.
